description:
Create, list, print, copy, delete and render notes. Every command names a note by its stem, the filename without .md, e.g. 2026-09-10-14-30-00.

Subcommands:
  new --type TYPE --topic TOPIC --thread THREAD [--thread THREAD ...] [--person NAME ...] [--counterparty X] [--location X] — create a note and print its path
  list [FILTER] [--json] — every note, oldest first: stem, date, type, threads, topic
  cat STEM — print a note
  last — print the path of the newest note
  copy STEM — copy a note to a new timestamp; ' COPY' is added to its topic
  delete STEM -y — permanently delete a note
  pdf STEM [--out DIR] — render to markdown and PDF, with callouts and an action table
  minutes STEM [--out DIR] — render meeting minutes: agreements, resolutions, action items
  agenda STEM [--out DIR] — render an agenda: the note with its outcome sections emptied

Args:
  STEM: note stem, from `notes list`. Stems are unique across the vault.
  FILTER: case-insensitive text matched against any column.

Flags:
  new:
    --type   required; one of Meeting, Correspondence, Workshop, Report, Log, Research, Recipe
    --topic TEXT   required; what the note is about
    --thread THREAD   required; thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink; repeatable. The note is filed under the first one.
    --person NAME   Meeting and Correspondence only; an attendee; repeatable; linked when people/<Name>.md exists
    --counterparty TEXT   Meeting only
    --location TEXT   Meeting only
  list:
    --json   JSON output
  delete:
    -y, --yes   required to confirm the delete
  pdf, minutes, agenda:
    --out DIR   output directory (default: the user's Downloads folder). Writes <stem>.md and <stem>.md.pdf and prints both paths.

Examples:
  ["new", "--type", "Meeting", "--topic", "Quarterly review", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--person", "Riaz Arbi"]
  ["list", "SGB", "--json"]
  ["cat", "2026-09-10-14-30-00"]
  ["minutes", "2026-09-10-14-30-00", "--out", "out"]

Notes:
  Notes are stored at threads/<Kind>/<Name>/notes/<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS>.md, under the first thread. `new` only creates the file. To add content, write the body into the path it prints.
  `new` also adds a REF: line to buffer.md, which reaches the thread's log on the next `buffer flush`.
  Every subcommand except `new` first ingests ACTION: lines into TASK: anchors, which rewrites note and log files in place.
  delete is permanent.
  pdf, minutes and agenda need pandoc and xelatex installed.
  Exit 1: --person on a type other than Meeting/Correspondence, --counterparty or --location on a non-Meeting note, empty --topic, a malformed stem, no notes in the vault, or a failed PDF render.
